## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the switch from `powerprofilesctl` to `busctl` + `jq` matches the power-profiles-daemon 0.30 D-Bus interface and systemd 262 `busctl` output. Profile order, the active marker, set semantics, error exits and polkit authorization are unchanged. One small behavior change in `Panel.qml` is described below, along with a note on test coverage.

| Path | Base (`powerprofilesctl`) | Head (`busctl`) |
|---|---|---|
| `omarchy-powerprofiles-list`, `--active-state`, menu provider | reference output | byte-identical in 5 synthetic daemon states (3- and 2-profile systems, each profile active) |
| `omarchy-powerprofiles-set` | reference exit, final profile, state files | identical in 5 scenarios (explicit, AC and battery defaults) |
| Profile order | daemon order, reversed by `powerprofilesctl list`, reversed back by `tac` | daemon order read directly (power-saver, balanced, performance) |
| Set denied or daemon missing | nonzero exit, no state written | nonzero exit, no state written |

The legacy `net.hadess.PowerProfiles` name is registered and D-Bus-activatable in 0.30, is still present on current upstream `main`, and the battery service already polls it. `busctl` defaults to the system bus, so the missing `--system` in `Menu.qml` targets the same bus. `jq` and systemd are base packages.

### `Panel.qml`: an empty refresh now clears the profile buttons

Base kept the last good profile list when a refresh returned nothing (the removed comment: "so the buttons don't blink out"). Base already re-queried on every open and every 5 s while the panel is open, so a failed read did not leave the list stuck.

```text
panel open, list shown ──► one refresh returns empty (daemon restart, failed read)
  base: keep last list ─────────────► next 5 s poll replaces it
  head: profiles = [], index = 0 ───► row empty until next 5 s poll;
                                      keyboard cursor returns to first profile
```

The added `if (profiles.length === 0) profilesProc.running = true` runs right after `refresh()` has started the same process. In Quickshell 0.3.1 `Process`, this does not start a second process. It queues one more run that starts as soon as the current one finishes, so on an open with an empty list, the query runs twice in a row. It does not add recovery on a later open (base already had that), and it does nothing for a later failed poll while the panel stays open.

**Impact:** small. With the `busctl` path, empty payloads should be rare. When one happens while the panel is open, the power-profile row disappears for up to about 5 s instead of staying usable. This follows from source; it was not observed on a desktop.

**Suggested change:** keep the existing last-good-list guard and drop this hunk (and its two regex assertions in `power-test.sh`), keeping the PR to the transport change. If a specific stuck state motivated it, describing that state would allow handling it directly, for example by clearing only after repeated empty payloads.

**Optional test improvement:** the new fake `busctl` in `powerprofiles-set-test.sh` matches only the verb and property keywords, so a wrong bus name, object path, interface, `s` signature or a missing `--json=short` would still pass. In a sandboxed run, the head test file against the base scripts with a working `powerprofilesctl` fake passed 11 of 12 assertions, and only the `rg 'powerprofilesctl'` source grep failed. Having the fake log its full argv and asserting the exact `get-property`/`set-property` lines for one list and one set call would tie the test to the new transport.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head `1047b804` against its merge-base, power-profiles-daemon 0.30 and current `main`, systemd v262 `busctl`, and Quickshell v0.3.1 `Process`. Sandboxed runs of `powerprofiles-set-test.sh` on head and base, plus base/head output comparisons, used synthetic `busctl` and `powerprofilesctl` fakes built from upstream source. No real daemon, system bus, polkit or hardware was used. `power-test.sh` was not executed (its new assertions were checked by source). Panel behavior was not observed in a running desktop session.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
